text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock fell slightly today, continuing a sharp decline from last week's peaks. The broader catalyst appears to be uncertainty about oil prices and refining margins—crude remains volatile amid Middle East tensions and geopolitical talk, while a potential diesel export ban could squeeze refiner profits by forcing production cuts without providing sustained pricing power. Refineries are running at 94% capacity with adequate inventory levels, so the weakness isn't driven by operational stress, but rather by policy risk and market confusion about where oil heads next.

The stock's 2.77% drop over two weeks coincides with oil's own wobbles and growing concern among energy investors about what policymakers will do. When political intervention in energy markets becomes a live question—whether export restrictions or responses to Middle East tensions—refiners often trade sideways or down until clarity emerges, regardless of their own operational strength.
